messages:
Maya R.: Heads-up — Brightwell wants to renew but says procurement only authorizes CC charges this cycle. They asked if we can accept a card fallback instead of the usual PO/wire.
Arjun P.: Hmm, renewal is $120k annually, right? CC fees will add ~3% unless we route through invoice split. @Lina G. any quick options? :thinking:
Lina G.: We can do a CC fallback but finance needs to know if they want full amount on card vs split (deposit on card, remainder invoiced). Deposit on card avoids PO but still needs SOW sign.
Maya R.: They explicitly said legal needs Docusign + billing via CC. Concerned about card limits for AMEX.
Tom (Legal): We can accept Docusign. For CC vs PO: need to confirm acceptance clause for auto-charge and refund policy in SOW. I can append an "invoice split" addendum template if needed.
Arjun P.: Timeline: customer wants to sign this week to hit FY close. If we need network approvals for >$75k on card it may delay.
Maya R.: Quote: 120,000 USD annual, start 2026-04-01. Proposal: take $20k on card as deposit, issue invoice for remaining $100k with 30d terms. That keeps them from raising PO now.
Lina G.: That works but finance flagged: if deposit on card, we need card reconciliation notes and VAT treatment — they're EU entity. Need EU billing entity id.
Maya R.: They are Brightwell EU (VAT: GB999888777). I mentioned to them we may need an invoice address and VAT number.
Tom (Legal): Also can we set a fallback payment clause: if card charge fails after x days, payment reverts to PO path and service may be paused. I'll draft clause: "If card fallback fails, Redwood will notify and revert to PO/wire; renewal date unaffected."
Arjun P.: Sounds solid. Quick check: do we need a vendor code for their PO if they later convert? Keep vendorcode field open.
Maya R.: They prefer not to issue PO this quarter. They asked if we could accept CC now and then provide PO later for accounting — basically retro-PO. Is that allowed? :grimacing:
Lina G.: Retro-PO is messy. We can accept CC now and permit them to raise a PO as record, but finance can't treat the PO as payment method. They must acknowledge card payment. We'll let them add PO number to invoice metadata.
Maya R.: Great. Customer asked about CC fee pass-through. Can we absorb fees or add a surcharge?
Arjun P.: Policy: we typically absorb up to $1k per payment for churn reasons on renewals under negotiation. For $120k, better to offer to absorb fees this once but add a note for future renewals.
Tom (Legal): If we absorb, add language "payment processing fees are borne by Redwood for this transaction only."
Maya R.: I'll send the SOW + addendum with deposit split, processing language, and VAT/invoice instructions. Will ping legal + finance to review before sending.
BillingBot: Invoice draft generated: invoice_2026_041_BW-01 (deposit $20,000 on CC). Link: https://billing.redwood/inv/invoice_2026_041_BW-01
Lina G.: Reviewing invoice now. ETA 90m.
Arjun P.: If finance clears, can we get a signoff step:
- Legal (Tom) approve addendum text
- Finance (Lina) confirm invoice/VAT details
- CS (Maya) send to customer
Maya R.: Yep. I'll hold sending until all green. Brightwell wants to sign by Fri EOD.
Tom (Legal): I'll drop the addendum in this thread when ready. :white_check_mark:
Lina G.: Invoice updated with VAT ID and PO metadata field. Ready pending legal.
Maya R.: Thanks team — I'll loop customer after legal drops clause. /cc @Tom (Legal) :pray:
Tom (Legal): Addendum posted: `https://docs.redwood/legal/addenda/cc-fallback-deposit-v1.docx` — small redlines suggested.
Maya R.: Reviewing now. If all good, I'll send SOW + invoice link + payment instructions with card fallback option.
Arjun P.: One more: set renewal flag in Salesforce to "pending-signature-cc" so AM gets visibility.
Maya R.: Done. Flag set.
BillingBot: Payment attempt scheduled for 2026-04-02 09:00 UTC (card on file).
Maya R.: Closing loop — will update thread after payment or if legal/finance need changes. :v:
